clue.text: Kit's tungsten withdrawn, following cut by Spain

indicators.note: withdrawn says the trimmed metal name is drawn back, read from right to left
cut says the letter for following is removed from the metal's name

parts.note: wolfram is the other name for the metal tungsten
f. is the standard abbreviation for following, as in page references
E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: Someone's kit has had its tungsten taken out after a Spanish cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kit' looks like equipment but is the playwright's nickname, and tungsten's older name is needed, not its symbol W. 'cut' and 'withdrawn' act in turn.
explanation.definitionFit: Christopher Marlowe, the Elizabethan playwright, was known to friends as Kit.

clue.text: Take out and beat up 11

indicators.note: in a down entry, up says the word is read bottom to top

parts.note: to drum is to beat
11 across is the queen whose cipher is ER, Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: A command to remove and thrash the queen of the eleventh entry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns DRUM to MURD; '11' is ELIZABETH I, whose royal cipher is ER.
explanation.definitionFit: Take out is slang for kill, as a hitman takes out a target.

clue.text: Butcher tried investing euros to make more trimmings

indicators.note: investing means surrounding, the mangled letters wrap the currency
to butcher something is to mangle it, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: E is the symbol for euros

explanation.surface: A butcher tried putting euros into the business to sell more trimmings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Butcher' looks like the meat trade; it turns TRIED into REDIT, 'investing' E after the R.
explanation.definitionFit: To re-edit a text is to cut it again, making further trims.

clue.text: Duck certain to go bad in very good style of ham

parts.note: a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, so O

indicators.note: in says the jumbled letters go inside VG
to go bad says the letters of certain are spoiled and rearranged

explanation.surface: A duck is sure to spoil in the very finest manner of cooking ham.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ham' suggests the meat, but a ham is a bad actor. 'to go bad' scrambles the fodder and 'in' places it.
explanation.definitionFit: A ham actor overplays his part, which is the manner of performing called overacting.

clue.text: Be certain to avoid river and come to pass

indicators.note: to avoid means the river letter is left out

parts.note: to ensure is to make certain

explanation.surface: Make sure to stay clear of the river, and then things will happen.
explanation.definitionFit: Ensue is a formal verb for follow or happen as a consequence.

clue.text: 10 left baffling sign

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship

indicators.note: baffling suggests the number word is confused, its letters jumbled

parts.note: the number is read simply as the word ten

explanation.surface: A puzzling clue pointing to the tenth entry leaves a cryptic sign behind.
explanation.walkthrough: '10' looks like a cross-reference to SHAKSPERE but is just the word TEN, which 'baffling' scrambles to ENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A portent is an omen, a sign of something about to happen.

clue.text: Theatre cast helps you pack in audience at the start

indicators.note: pack in says the jumbled letters cram the first letter of audience inside
cast suggests throwing the letters about to form a new order
at the start picks the opening letter of audience

explanation.surface: At a theatre, the cast helps you squeeze into the audience at the start of the show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast' scrambles HELPS YOU, and 'pack in' sets A, the first letter of 'audience', third.
explanation.definitionFit: A playhouse is a building where plays are staged, a theatre.

clue.text: 5 down went up

definitions.meaning: an Elizabethan playhouse on Bankside in London
went up means ascended, the past tense of rise

explanation.surface: The theatre was built.
explanation.walkthrough: '5 down' is PLAYHOUSE; the Rose staged Marlowe's plays.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rose was a Bankside theatre, and the past tense of rise means ascended.

clue.text: Ditzy Essex girl hands out drug first for analysis

indicators.note: first says the drug letter heads the answer

parts.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy

indicators.note: ditzy means scatterbrained, so the letters are scrambled
out says the letters for the two hands are removed

parts.note: R and L are right and left, the two hands

explanation.surface: A scatty girl from Essex hands out drugs before an analysis.
explanation.walkthrough: An 'Essex girl' is a British stereotype of a brash young woman. 'out' strips RL from ESSEXGIRL; 'Ditzy' rearranges ESSEXGI to XEGESIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Exegesis is critical interpretation of a text, especially scripture: a form of analysis.

clue.text: Two and three, possibly 11 penned here

indicators.note: possibly says the letters could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Two or three people might have been writing here.
explanation.walkthrough: 'penned' suggests writing but means imprisoned; '11' is ELIZABETH I, held in the Tower of London under her sister Mary.
explanation.definitionFit: Princess Elizabeth was imprisoned in the Tower of London in 1554, so she was confined there.

clue.text: Old official leading ladies, first one retired

indicators.note: the first of the two ladies is retired, which here means turned back to front

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the queen, a leading lady
Eve was the first woman, another leading lady

explanation.surface: An official of old walks ahead of the leading ladies, one of whom has stepped down.
explanation.walkthrough: The Queen (Elizabeth Regina) and the first woman are both leading ladies; 'first one retired' turns only the Queen's cipher.
explanation.definitionFit: A reeve was a medieval local officer, such as a manor overseer or a shire's magistrate.

clue.text: Will (early version) speaks vaguely about burying Henry

indicators.note: burying says the letter for Henry is sunk inside the jumbled word
vaguely says the word speaks is rendered loosely, its letters rearranged

parts.note: H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: Someone talks hazily about a buried man called Henry, as an early form of a will.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Will' is the man, not a legal document. 'vaguely' scrambles the fodder to SAKSPE and 'burying' sinks H after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakspere is one of the old spellings of the playwright William's surname found in early documents.

clue.text: The brazil nuts run out in middle of seeing 10's patron

indicators.note: in says the scrambled letters sit inside the central pair
the middle of seeing is its central pair of letters
nuts means crazy, so the letters are thrown into a new order
out says the letter for run leaves the word brazil

parts.note: R is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Brazil nuts that have run out, seen in the middle of the playwright's patron's larder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' removes R from BRAZIL; 'nuts' scrambles THE plus BAZIL into LIZABETH, which goes 'in' EI, the middle of 'seeing'.
explanation.definitionFit: The queen was the reigning monarch and patron of the theatre when Shakespeare wrote; her favour sustained his company.

clue.text: Swimmer's objective? A girl's love

parts.note: her is the possessive for a girl
love is nil in tennis, written as O

explanation.surface: A girl wonders what a swimmer is aiming for and what she loves.
explanation.walkthrough: In legend Leander swam the Hellespont nightly to reach his lover; Marlowe wrote the poem about them.
explanation.definitionFit: Leander's goal on each nightly swim across the strait was his beloved, the priestess of Aphrodite.

clue.text: Coppers seize set and very large amount of fake curtains

indicators.note: seize says the coins grip the word for set between them

parts.note: p is a penny, and pennies are coppers
to lay is to set down
OS is the clothing abbreviation for outsize
a sum is an amount

explanation.surface: Police grab a theatrical set and a large amount of counterfeit curtains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coppers' suggests police, but means pennies, PP. 'curtains' is slang for death, so 'fake curtains' means feigning death.
explanation.definitionFit: To play possum is to pretend to be dead, as the opossum does when threatened.

clue.text: End of dentist's drill left in a state, 1 across's 12

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter
in says the drill and left go inside the state

parts.note: Maine is a US state
a bur, or burr, is a dentist's small drill bit

explanation.surface: The dentist's drill is the last straw, left in a state over a fellow's hero.
explanation.walkthrough: BURL goes 'in' A MAINE, after the M, with T from 'dentist's' first.
explanation.definitionFit: Tamburlaine the Great is Marlowe's play, its title character the conquering protagonist.

clue.text: Recall study analysing income in so-called store

indicators.note: in says the reordered letters go inside the store's letters

parts.note: Marks and Spencer, a British chain store, is often called M and S, or M 'n' S

indicators.note: analysing means breaking down, so the letters of income are separated and reordered

explanation.surface: A study recalls analysing income in a particular store.
explanation.walkthrough: Marks & Spencer is a British department store, colloquially M 'n' S; 'analysing' scrambles the fodder and 'in' sets it after the second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Mnemonics is the study and craft of devices that aid memory and recall.

clue.text: Relatives' regal reforms in 10's work

parts.note: kin are relatives

indicators.note: reforms means shapes anew, so the letters of regal are rearranged

explanation.surface: The family's royal reforms appear in a dramatist's work.
explanation.definitionFit: King Lear is one of Shakespeare's tragedies, a work of the playwright.

clue.text: Display set and decor under guard

indicators.note: to display is to arrange on show, so the letters are set out anew

explanation.surface: A stage set and its decoration are shown off while protected.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone escorted is accompanied by guards, kept under protection.

clue.text: Lacking honesty, popular bank's taken over because …

indicators.note: taken over places the word for bank after the word for because, as if it had taken it over

parts.note: in means fashionable, popular
since means because
to bank on something is to rely on it

explanation.surface: A dishonest takeover: a popular bank has been bought out, and the clue trails off to explain why.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis runs on into 21 across, a surface link only.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something insincerely means doing it without honesty or genuine feeling.

clue.text: Airport area overlooks a royal 1 across and 10?

indicators.note: overlooks means misses out, so the named letters are dropped

parts.note: arrivals is the airport area for incoming passengers
R stands for royal, as in RN

explanation.surface: An airport lounge looks down on a royal visitor, two playwrights among the crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overlooks' suggests a view but means ignores, dropping A and R from the front of ARRIVALS.
explanation.definitionFit: Marlowe and Shakespeare were contemporaries and competitors for the London stage.

clue.text: 5 dances about, carousing

indicators.note: about says the dances wrap round the numeral

parts.note: reels are lively Scottish dances
V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: Five people dance about while partying.
explanation.walkthrough: '5' looks like a cross-reference but is the Roman numeral V.
explanation.definitionFit: Revels are boisterous festivities, the noisy merrymaking of a party.

clue.text: … 5 down limited a little stable liquidity

indicators.note: limited says the theatre's name is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: the Globe was the playhouse where Shakespeare's company performed

explanation.surface: Following on from the previous clue: the theatre's funds were restricted, leaving a little steady cash.
explanation.walkthrough: '5 down' is PLAYHOUSE; the playhouse meant is the Globe in London.
explanation.definitionFit: A glob is a small blob of thick liquid that holds its shape.

clue.text: Firm undertaking restricts money settlement

parts.note: Co. is short for company, a firm
an undertaking is a promise

explanation.surface: A company's pledge limits how much cash goes into a deal.
explanation.definitionFit: A compromise is an agreement reached by each side giving ground, a settlement.

clue.text: 26 down, up

indicators.note: in a down entry, up says the words read from bottom to top

parts.note: down is the opposite of up, so not up

explanation.walkthrough: '26 down' looks like a cross-reference; the definition is just '26', STAGE, and 'down' is the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To stage a play is to put it on, to present it in performance.

clue.text: A selection of the best evergreen shrubs

indicators.note: A selection of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A gardener picks out only the finest evergreen bushes.
explanation.definitionFit: Hebe is a genus of evergreen flowering bushes from New Zealand, widely planted in gardens.

clue.text: Fanatic to survive bracing term at sea

indicators.note: bracing says the verb holds the jumbled letters within it

parts.note: to exist is to survive

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the word term is jumbled

explanation.surface: A fanatic hopes to survive a bracing spell at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bracing' sounds like a sea breeze but means holding; 'at sea' scrambles the word term.
explanation.definitionFit: An extremist holds radical views, much as a zealot or fanatic does.

clue.text: Leg gets a wound

indicators.note: wound, as in wound up or twisted, says the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone's leg receives a wound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wound' reads as an injury but is the past of wind, twisting GETS A into a new order.
explanation.definitionFit: A stage of a journey or race is one section of it, just as a leg is.

clue.text: Embarrassed dealing with Sunday school compensation

parts.note: an embarrassed face turns red
re means concerning, dealing with
SS is the abbreviation for Sunday school

explanation.surface: An embarrassed teacher is handling a Sunday school's claim for damages.
explanation.definitionFit: Redress is a remedy or reparation for a wrong, a form of compensation.

clue.text: I seem torn between extremes — it's my undoing

indicators.note: between says the jumbled letters sit inside the two poles

parts.note: north and south, N and S, are the poles, the extremes of the globe

indicators.note: torn means ripped apart, so the letters of I seem are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone torn between two extremes admits this indecision will be their downfall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'torn' turns I SEEM into EMESI, set 'between' N and S.
explanation.definitionFit: A nemesis is the agent of someone's downfall, the force that brings ruin.
